families.name: Medium-voltage power
families.desc: 5/8 kV, 15 kV and 35 kV MV-105 constructions for plant feeders, source and tie circuits, collectors and transformer feeds. Select the construction from the actual system voltage, insulation level and routing design.

families.name: Low-voltage distribution and motor feeders
families.desc: 600 V and 600/1000 V EPR-insulated singles and multiconductor tray-rated feeders for secondaries, motors, panels and equipment.

families.name: VFD cable
families.desc: Shielded drive-output constructions, flexible or armored, matched to the drive system. Qualify the drive before selecting the cable.

families.name: Control and instrumentation
families.desc: CT/VT and breaker-control multiconductors, shielded pairs and triads for analog, status, RTD and thermocouple circuits, and armored instrumentation for classified areas. Type TC and TC-ER are distinct ratings.

families.name: Flexible, portable and approved DC applications
families.desc: DLO flexible power for emergency and battery circuits, and RenewaFLEX for approved internal BESS wiring. Fixed wiring and portable cable are different applications; BESS DC is not solar PV.

families.name: Grounding and bonding
families.desc: Bare copper and insulated equipment grounds for the ground grid, equipment bonds and shield grounds. Final sizes follow the grounding study.

families.name: Communications, building systems and specialty
families.desc: Fiber and industrial networks, building-system and branch wiring, switchboard wire, terminations and accessories, and OEM or special-environment leads that follow equipment specifications.

zones.name: Switchyard / GSU / grid tie
zones.package: Station service and protection cable package
zones.cable: LV station service; CT/VT and breaker-control cable; trip/close DC; protection fiber; ground grid and equipment bonds.
zones.focus: Define utility and GSU boundaries. HV underground cable is a separate engineered scope.
zones.buys: EPC / substation contractor via distribution; owner standards and utility team influence.

decision.title: One agreed grid handoff
decision.cables: Selected HV underground or overhead conductor; station service; battery trip/close; CT/VT, relay and SCADA circuits; ground grid and utility-approved fiber.
decision.release: Confirm ownership, voltage, terminals, sheath bonding, ground-potential interfaces and diverse protection routes. Select OPGW or ADSS only when the overhead communications architecture requires it.

zones.name: Battery energy storage
zones.cable: RenewaFLEX for approved internal BESS wiring; MV collectors; PCS AC links; BMS/control, data and grounding.
zones.focus: 13892403 is a 4/0, 2 kV BESS reference. 66131915 is a 35 kV EPR-insulated collector candidate only where the project design calls for it. Separate internal DC wiring from field AC scope.
zones.buys: BESS integrator owns internal design; EPC buys field AC, collector and site connections.

decision.title: Four systems within one fence
decision.cables: Approved field DC using RenewaFLEX or DLO; PCS AC; selected MV collection; and auxiliary, BMS, fire, fiber and grounding circuits.
decision.release: Fix DC polarity/fault duty, connector and crimp compatibility, collector voltage and the factory-to-field boundary. Container count does not establish cable footage; do not add internal battery harnesses by default.

zones.name: Reel staging / prefab
zones.package: Cable delivery and assembly work packages
zones.cable: All destination-zone cable families; circuit labels, reel/cut lists, bundles, kits and installation documentation.
zones.focus: Offer preterminated assemblies only to an agreed engineered scope. Staging adds no circuit footage.
zones.buys: EPC construction, electrical contractor and distributor; assembly scope with the qualified packager.

decision.title: Build the route into the package
decision.cables: Segregated MV/LV/control/fiber routes, ground continuity, penetrations, spare pathways and circuit-to-reel assignments.
decision.release: Reconcile source-to-destination lengths, thermal conditions, fill, bends, pull direction, tension and sidewall pressure. Confirm end seals, access and firestop responsibility. Shared tray or duct length is not additional cable footage.

zones.name: Admin / control room
zones.cable: MV/LV supply; UPS interfaces; SIMpull THHN/THWN-2 branch wire; applicable Genesis building systems; data and grounding.
zones.focus: Select fire alarm, security and network listings by system; qualify plant OS2 fiber separately.
zones.buys: EPC / electrical contractor for feeds; controls integrator and low-voltage contractor for systems.

decision.title: Make power and controls fit
decision.cables: MV/LV feeders, VFD outputs, UPS/DC, relay control, instrument trunks, OS2 fiber and building-system cable.
decision.release: Align cable OD, bend space, conductor class, lugs and terminal limits. Define CT/VT circuits, shield bonding and diverse protection paths. Use listed circuit-integrity systems only for compatible fire-alarm/communications duty.

zones.name: E-house
zones.package: Primary distribution and factory interface package
zones.cable: 5 kV or 15 kV-class MV source/tie feeders; Royal Guard LV secondaries; control, protection, DC, data and bonding.
zones.focus: MV examples: 55052299 (5/8 kV) and 55050899 (15 kV). Confirm the one-line and separate OEM internal wiring from EPC field connections.
zones.buys: E-house / switchgear OEM for internal wiring; EPC / distributor for field feeders and ties.

services.name: Construction Planning Services
services.desc: Takeoffs, BOMs, field drawings, coordination and pull calculations. Qualify circuit marking, pull heads and bundling against the installation sequence.

services.name: CableTechSupport
services.desc: Application review for construction and application questions before the specification freezes.

services.name: SPEED Services
services.desc: Qualified custom requests and schedule needs.

services.name: Project Services
services.desc: Coordination, marking, kitting, labels and bundles packaged around the installation sequence.

services.name: Reel tracking
services.desc: Qualify reel tracking, pull lengths and staged issue with the project team.

services.name: Contractor Solutions & SIMpull
services.desc: Bring the field team into route layouts, pull calculations and equipment setup. Align handling, pulling and crew preparation before cable arrives.

services.name: Field Assessment & rejuvenation
services.desc: Evaluate existing underground systems with Field Assessment Services. For eligible aging cable, assess rejuvenation alongside repair or replacement and the planned outage window.

grid.name: Underground transmission
grid.desc: Southwire's published 69–500 kV scope includes cable systems, accessories, engineering, installation and testing. Qualify voltage, route, bonding, terminations and the utility interface.

grid.name: Overhead gen-tie & grid upgrades
grid.desc: Compare conventional conductors with C7 composite-core options when thermal capacity, span, sag or reconductoring drives the design. Final selection belongs to the line engineer and utility.

applications.name: Combined cycle, simple cycle & peakers
applications.desc: Plant MV distribution, turbine auxiliaries, HRSG instruments, cooling motors and switchyard protection. A simple-cycle plant has a different balance of plant.

applications.name: RICE, fuel cells & onsite power
applications.desc: Separate internal OEM wiring from yard feeders, starting/DC circuits, controls and grounding. For data centers, microgrids and industrial CHP, confirm the generation-to-campus handoff.

applications.name: BESS & hybrid sites
applications.desc: Distinguish internal battery wiring, field DC interconnects and AC collector feeders. Confirm voltage, polarity, terminals, fire requirements and the integrator's approved cable design.

applications.name: Brownfield upgrades & new process loads
applications.desc: Assess aging feeders and outage windows. Add a separate motor and instrument schedule for carbon capture, water treatment or cooling expansion; verify spare route and switchgear capacity.

cases.tag: Custom MV cable / Canadian metals & mining
cases.title: From RFQ to shipment.
cases.problem: An unusual MV construction and quantity against a 20-week reference lead time.
cases.contribution: Custom MV cable engineered and manufactured to the project's requirement.
cases.result: Southwire reports shipment in 15 weeks against a 20-week reference, with a 33% reduction in minimum order quantity.
cases.powergen: Bring cable engineering in early for unusual e-house, ACC or process-feeder constructions and quantities.

cases.title: Rejuvenated at Dayton Airport.
cases.problem: Aging MV feeders with a replacement estimate and a limited outage window.
cases.contribution: Cable rejuvenation of the existing feeders in place.
cases.result: Southwire reports $530,161 saved against estimated replacement cost, with the feeder project completed in two months.
cases.powergen: Assess rejuvenation for suitable aging MV feeders during brownfield life-extension planning.

cases.tag: Field installation / BJC West County Hospital
cases.title: A coordinated installation setup.
cases.problem: Sixteen feeder pulls of 220–230 feet with large parallel conductors on a working site.
cases.contribution: Pull calculations, reel setup and coordinated equipment planning with Contractor Solutions and SIMpull equipment.
cases.result: Southwire documents 16 pulls of 220–230 feet using 4 × 750 kcmil aluminum conductors with ground.
cases.powergen: Use pull calculations, reel setup and coordinated equipment planning for auxiliary feeders. Confirm the actual route and conductor construction.

cases.title: High-voltage cable, manufactured and installed.
cases.problem: An onshore high-voltage cable system for a generation project's grid connection.
cases.contribution: Design, manufacturing and installation of the project's onshore high-voltage cable system.
cases.result: Southwire's case study describes design, manufacturing and installation of the project's onshore high-voltage cable system.
cases.powergen: Engage the HV team early when a generation project requires a qualified underground gen-tie or grid connection.

cases.title: Replacement cost deferred.
cases.problem: A large population of aging underground distribution cable.
cases.contribution: A multi-year rejuvenation program described in a Southwire-hosted paper.
cases.result: The paper reports over 12 million conductor feet rejuvenated through 2020 and the utility's estimate of more than $800 million in deferred replacement cost.
cases.powergen: Use condition assessment to compare rejuvenation, repair and replacement for eligible aging plant feeders. Utility program results are not a forecast for a generation site.

cases.title: A 69 kV underground circuit kept in service.
cases.problem: A 1,300-foot underground 69 kV section originally installed in 1969.
cases.contribution: Rejuvenation of the existing 500 kcmil aluminum, 69 kV XLPE cable.
cases.result: Southwire's paper describes rejuvenation of the section rather than replacement.
cases.powergen: For suitable brownfield circuits, evaluate cable condition, accessories and outage requirements before choosing rejuvenation or replacement.

checklist: One-line, system voltage, load and fault data, circuit schedule, grounding and redundancy requirements.

lifecycle.name: Start with the circuit record
lifecycle.desc: Establish cable construction, joints, terminations, loading, route and failure consequence. Use an agreed assessment program to distinguish localized defects from distributed aging; retain comparable baseline results.

lifecycle.name: Qualify repair before replacement
lifecycle.desc: Southwire Re³ kits address eligible insulation/jacket damage on specified products. Damaged conductors or compromised armor are outside the kit scope. Follow the manufacturer method and project acceptance requirements. Published codes 67037340 / 67037640.

lifecycle.name: Screen rejuvenation eligibility
lifecycle.desc: Evaluate cable construction, condition, neutral/shield integrity, accessories and future loading. Compare rejuvenation, targeted repair and replacement with the owner's outage plan; confirm eligibility and warranty terms.

lifecycle.name: EPIC HPFF retrofit
lifecycle.desc: For an existing high-pressure fluid-filled cable system, review Southwire's engineered solid-dielectric replacement using existing pipe infrastructure. Scope depends on pipe condition, thermal duty, pulls and termination transitions.

boundaries.name: Separate cable from bus systems
boundaries.desc: Treat generator-to-GSU isolated-phase bus, GCB/GIS and busway as equipment interfaces where selected. A cable alternate replaces a defined segment only after ampacity, fault-force, loss, cooling and OEM review. HV underground is a complete cable/accessory/bonding system; overhead conductor and line communications follow the utility basis.

boundaries.name: Retain the proprietary interfaces
boundaries.desc: Track probe/coax leads, vibration/speed pickups, ignition, flame scanners, excitation leads, CEMS composite umbilicals, heat-trace elements and true reeling/festoon cable separately. Obtain vendor part numbers, temperatures, impedance, bend/flex duty and terminations. Schedule the assigned field feeders without duplicating package internals.

boundaries.name: Qualify each complete system
boundaries.desc: Fire/gas detection, alarm, releasing, emergency power and fire-pump feeders have different duties. Circuit Defender applies only to compatible listed alarm/communications systems; it is not general motor or fire-pump power cable. Select OS2, industrial copper, OPGW or ADSS by actual link, route and owner requirements.

boundaries.name: One quantity basis per release
boundaries.desc: Keep model route length, installed cable length, procurement allowance and copper weight separate. Reconcile model and schedule by circuit ID; do not add their totals. Mark rows as base, conditional addition, replacement alternate or separate takeoff. Exclude duplicated trunks, grounding components, factory wiring and temporary test leads.

steps: One-line, load/fault data, system voltage, grounding, insulation level, route exposure, redundancy and OEM / utility boundaries.
Conductor / size / parallels, shield and jacket, listings, accessories, bend space and terminal fit. Compare substitutions field by field.
Thermal inputs, ampacity, voltage drop, duct / tray fill, pull tension and sidewall pressure. Assign cut length, reel, pull direction and route-ready date.
Approved quantities and exceptions; quoted stock / packaging, dated price and metal basis, lead time, freight, storage, labeling and delivery sequence.
Agreed test method / acceptance, reel and accessory IDs, pull / torque records, polarity and loop checks, as-builts, spares and operating baseline.
